intent: Specify the public API of `fixedbitset::FixedBitSet` (fixedbitset 0.4.2): `new`, `with_capacity`, `grow`, `len`, `is_empty`, `contains`, `insert`, `put`, `toggle`, `set`, `copy_bit`, `set_range`, `insert_range`, `toggle_range`, `as_slice` (Lean: `fixedbitset.FixedBitSet.<name>`; `&mut self` methods return the updated set, `put` returns `(previous, set)`). The range methods take an `IndexRange` instance and a range value; the crate's instances are `core.ops.range.Range.Insts.FixedbitsetRangeIndexRange core.Usize.Insts.CoreMarkerCopy` (value `{ start := a, «end» := b }`), `core.ops.range.RangeFrom.Insts.FixedbitsetRangeIndexRange core.Usize.Insts.CoreMarkerCopy` (`{ start := a }`), `core.ops.range.RangeTo.Insts.FixedbitsetRangeIndexRange core.Usize.Insts.CoreMarkerCopy` (`{ «end» := b }`) and `core.ops.range.RangeFull.Insts.FixedbitsetRangeIndexRange Std.Usize` (value `()`), all in namespace `fixedbitset`.

manual_mutants.note: range end equal to the length is rejected (full-length ranges panic)
last-block mask off by one (the last bit of a range is not covered / one extra bit)
an empty final mask is still yielded: ranges ending on a block boundary touch a nonexistent block
put returns the negated previous value
copy_bit reads the destination instead of the source
grow fills new blocks with ones
with_capacity drops the partial block when len % 32 == 1

sibling_mutants.note: with_capacity keeps one spare (zero) block: as_slice is one block longer, no observable bit differs
sibling_mutants.after: let blocks1 ← (do let t ← blocks + i; t + 1#usize)

bug_variants.note: before 'Check bit length more correctly', insert and set indexed the block vector directly without checking bit < len: a bit in [len, 32*blocks) is silently set (contains then reports a bit outside the capacity) instead of panicking as documented ('Panics if bit is out of bounds'). Ported to the 0.4.2 extraction by removing the length assertion (the remaining slice access still panics past the last block, like the pre-fix `self.data[block]`).
